profiles.name: CI test fixture
profiles.description: Synthetic 200-point fixture used by CI tests.

profiles.name: DE Utility Solar PV Capacity Factor 2019
profiles.description: Hourly capacity-factor profile for utility-scale solar PV in Germany. Based on Fraunhofer ISE 2020 PV status report (target CF 11.3%, 2019). Generated from ERA5-calibrated diurnal×seasonal model with synoptic cloud variability.

profiles.name: DE Rooftop Solar PV Capacity Factor 2019
profiles.source: HTW Berlin Yield Study / ERA5 Synthetic
profiles.description: Hourly capacity-factor profile for rooftop solar PV (south-facing, 30° tilt) in Germany. Based on HTW Berlin annual yield study (target CF ~9.8%, 2019). Slightly lower than utility due to suboptimal orientation and shading losses.

profiles.name: ES Utility Solar PV Capacity Factor 2019
profiles.source: IRENA Renewable Power Generation Costs 2020 / ERA5 Synthetic
profiles.description: Hourly capacity-factor profile for utility-scale single-axis tracking PV in Spain. IRENA 2020 reports 20-22% average CF for Iberian peninsula. Target: 20.5%.

profiles.name: IT Utility Solar PV Capacity Factor 2019
profiles.description: Hourly capacity-factor profile for utility-scale PV in Italy (central/northern). IRENA 2020 Italian average CF: ~17%. Target: 17.0%.

profiles.name: GR Utility Solar PV Capacity Factor 2019
profiles.description: Hourly capacity-factor profile for utility-scale PV in Greece. IRENA 2020: Greece average CF ~22%. Target: 22.0%.

profiles.name: DE Onshore Wind Capacity Factor 2019
profiles.description: Hourly capacity-factor profile for onshore wind in Germany. Fraunhofer IEE Windmonitor 2020: German fleet CF 21.5% in 2019. Strong winter peak, synoptic 3-7 day variability.

profiles.name: DE Offshore Wind (North Sea) Capacity Factor 2019
profiles.description: Hourly capacity-factor profile for North Sea offshore wind in Germany. Fraunhofer IEE: offshore fleet CF 37% in 2019. Higher base load factor and stronger seasonal amplitude than onshore.

profiles.name: DK Offshore Wind Capacity Factor 2019
profiles.description: Hourly capacity-factor profile for Danish offshore wind (Horns Rev, Anholt fleet). Energinet.dk 2019 average fleet CF: ~42.5%. Best offshore wind resource in Europe.

profiles.name: UK Offshore Wind Capacity Factor 2019
profiles.description: Hourly capacity-factor profile for UK offshore wind (North Sea & Irish Sea combined). BEIS Energy Trends 2019: fleet average ~40%. Typical Atlantic storm tracks produce strong winter output.

profiles.name: FR Onshore Wind Capacity Factor 2019
profiles.description: Hourly capacity-factor profile for onshore wind in France. RTE Bilan Électrique 2019: French onshore fleet CF ~24.5%. Regional spread from Brittany (Atlantic) to Mediterranean.

profiles.name: DE Total Electricity Demand 2019
profiles.description: Hourly total net electricity consumption for Germany 2019. OPSD annual total: 490 TWh → annual average 55.9 GW. Weekday/weekend pattern, seasonal (winter-higher) envelope, morning ramp (06-09h) and evening peak (18-21h).

profiles.name: DE Residential Electricity Demand 2019
profiles.source: OPSD / BDEW Standard Load Profiles Synthetic
profiles.description: Hourly household electricity demand for Germany. Represents the H0 standard load profile from BDEW. Strong evening peak (21h), lower weekend demand. Annual share ~30% of total: avg ~16.8 GW.

profiles.name: DE Industrial Electricity Demand 2019
profiles.description: Hourly industrial electricity consumption for Germany. Based on BDEW G1 (weekday-heavy industry) load profile. Flat during operating hours (06-22h), greatly reduced weekends. Annual share ~38% of total: avg ~21.3 GW.

profiles.name: FR Total Electricity Demand 2019
profiles.description: Hourly total electricity consumption for France 2019. RTE annual total: ~472 TWh → avg 53.9 GW. France has higher winter peak than Germany due to electric heating (effet joule).

profiles.name: UK Total Electricity Demand 2019
profiles.description: Hourly total electricity demand for Great Britain 2019. National Grid ESO: ~319 TWh → avg 36.5 GW. Moderate winter heating driven peak, strong daylight/evening pattern.

profiles.name: DE Hydro Run-of-River Capacity Factor 2019
profiles.description: Hourly capacity-factor profile for run-of-river hydro in Germany (primarily Bavaria/Rhine). Fraunhofer IEE: German RoR fleet CF ~45% in 2019. Spring snowmelt peak (April-May), drier late-summer trough.

profiles.name: AT Alpine Hydro Capacity Factor 2019
profiles.description: Hourly capacity-factor profile for Austrian alpine hydro (reservoir + RoR combined). Verbund 2019 annual report: fleet average CF ~38%. High latitude Alpine snowpack drives pronounced spring-summer season.

profiles.name: NO Hydro Reservoir Capacity Factor 2019
profiles.description: Hourly capacity-factor profile for Norwegian reservoir hydro. NVE 2020: Norwegian fleet CF ~49%. Covers dispatchable reservoir plants. Snowmelt peak in May-June; operators store water over autumn/winter.

profiles.name: DE/AT/LU Day-Ahead Electricity Price 2019
profiles.description: Hourly day-ahead spot electricity price for the DE/AT/LU bidding zone (EPEX SPOT). EPEX 2019 annual average: 37.7 EUR/MWh. Includes negative price events (high VRE + low demand weekends), winter morning spikes, and residual-demand-driven price formation.

profiles.name: FR Day-Ahead Electricity Price 2019
profiles.description: Hourly day-ahead spot price for France (EPEX SPOT FR). EPEX 2019 FR annual average: 39.5 EUR/MWh. Nuclear-dominated baseload with fuel-cost driven variation and demand-driven winter peaks from electric heating.

profiles.name: DE Global Horizontal Irradiance 2019
profiles.description: Hourly global horizontal irradiance (GHI) for Germany, averaged over the country. ERA5 / DWD data for 2019: annual sum ~1100 kWh/m². Used for solar yield calculations and PV model validation.

profiles.name: DE Wind Speed at 100 m Hub Height 2019
profiles.description: Hourly wind speed at 100 m hub height, spatially averaged for Germany. ERA5 2019 mean at 100 m: ~6.8 m/s. Used for wind turbine power curve calculations and repowering studies.
